src.by: the Spa survey window (a separate Claude Code session), 2026-11-27 – the user's request
src.imagery: Service public de Wallonie (SPW) orthophotos, 0.25 m a pixel, Belgian Lambert 72 (EPSG:31370), CC BY 4.0, read on their own pixel grid (geoservices.wallonie.be IMAGERIE/ORTHO_*): "Orthophotos 2026 - Printemps" flown 2026-04-07 10:46 UTC (sun 45 deg high at 161 deg), "Orthophotos 2025 - Printemps" 2025-04-29 14:27 UTC (40 deg at 240 deg), "Orthophotos 2024" 2024-09-01 09:24 UTC (38 deg at 137 deg, the sharpest). All three measured, each on its own; the service's stated accuracy 0.25 … 0.54 m. Looked at and measured only.
src.not_used: Esri World Imagery here is a WorldView-2 satellite picture of 2025-06-22: 0.5 m a pixel, stated accuracy 8.5 m
src.coordinates: [lat, lon] = ETRS89 (as the web maps take it for WGS84), from Lambert 72 by the exact conic formulas and the national grid of shifts BD72 → ETRS89 (bd72lb72_etrs89lb08, NGI/IGN Belgium); it agrees with the 7-parameter transformation (EPSG:15929) within 0.05 m here. Widths and lengths in this file are ground metres on the ellipsoid.
src.method: The track straightened along a guide down its middle (a row every 0.5 m, 0.05 m across, cubic interpolation of the 0.25 m pixels). Each side: the first white line met walking out from the middle, followed round the lap on the three years together – a bright step that is there in one year only is a shadow or a wall's leaning top, not a line. Then in each year by itself the line's INNER face (the half-height point of the rise from tarmac to white, on the least of the three colours) and its OUTER face (where the white of paint ends: least colour less the colours' spread, which tells a white line from a kerb's red and yellow, green paint and concrete); each year's blur taken off (0.04 / 0.09 / 0.01 m a face). The older photos' sideways offsets from the 2026 one are found from the lines themselves and taken out; the inner face is the middle value of the years; the edge given is inner face + the line's own width as measured nearby (30th percentile over ±5 m of outer − inner: 0.32 m in the middle of the lap's values, 0.23 … 0.41) = the white line's OUTER face. Finally the edges are put at the middle of the three photos' places. Checked by eye on all three years round the whole lap (300 m sheets), and closer at La Source, the two pit lane ends, the Bus Stop and every stretch where the years disagreed.

years_against_each_other.what: the same face read in two years, after each photo's own sideways offset is taken out (rows of 0.5 m, both sides)

line_not_seen.what: sections [from, to] where no year gave a reading over 2 m or more and the edge was carried straight across from either side (all shorter than 4 m)

band_wider_than_a_line.what: sections where the white band beside the tarmac is wider than 0.45 m all along (a pale strip or gutter lies against the line and cannot be told from it at 0.25 m a pixel): the edge given is the band's inner face + 0.32 m (a line's width) – the white itself ends up to 0.35 m further out

notes: RIGHT, sections 86 … 105 (after the pit exit, beside the old pit lane's first wall): a wall about 1 m high stands 0.3 m behind the white line. In the 2025 and 2026 photos its shadow lies over the line and its top leans 0.2 m over it (the camera stood to the west), so the first bright thing there is the wall, 0.1 … 0.5 m further out; only the 2024 photo shows the line itself, and the edge is read from it alone. Further on (to section 144) the line shows in 2026 and 2024 alike.

The 2026 photo (7 April) was taken during work before the season: besides the stretch in `low`, on the RIGHT at sections 898 … 905 (Blanchimont) a strip of new tarmac lies along the kerb with no line on it yet. There the edge is the line of 2024 and 2025 (the years' middle value).
Kemmel (joins.support_pit_exit): a solid line of the support races' pit exit runs inside the track; the edge given is the track's own outer line.
On the start straight a strip of grass about 3 m wide lies between the right edge line and the pit wall: the edge is the line.

Lines across the whole track, metres after the control line along the middle (not marks, for reference): start line 122.1; pit exit lane end 364.4; others at about 187, 374, 818, 1636, 1664, 6574, 6868 (shadows of bridges and gantries left out).

read_in_one_year_only.what: sections where one photo alone shows the line (the others: shadow, or a wall's shadow and leaning top over it)

marks_note.start: the start line (0.4 m thick), its two ends on the track's edges [left, right]
marks_note.control: the finish (control) line: a band 1.0 m thick across the track, its middle; 122.1 m before the start line (the published offset of this circuit is 0.124 km)
marks_note.pole: the front line of pole's grid box [its left end, its right end]: on the RIGHT of the track (the pit side), 2.0 m behind the start line; the box is 2.9 m wide, its right end 2.5 m from the right edge, its left end 9.7 m from the left edge. The second box is on the left, 8.0 m behind pole's.

pit_entry.what: the mouth of the pit entry road at the Bus Stop: the track's edge line is broken here (dashes over about 9 m) and the entry road leaves to the right between them; the edge given runs straight through the dashes

pit_exit.what: the pit exit lane comes round the inside of La Source and lies against the track from the tip of the green triangle; between these sections edges.right is the solid line between the lane and the track (its lane side). At the line across (the lane's end, 0.33 m thick, just after ends_at_section) the lane ends: from the next section the track's edge is the lane's own far line, about 5 m further out – the two sections either side of the step are 5 m apart. road_right: the lane's far edge (the outer face of its right-hand line) at the sections road_right_sections.

support_pit_exit.what: Kemmel: the support races' pit exit road joins from the right about 45 m after the first of these sections, and a solid white line runs INSIDE the track from the tip of the red paint to a line across the track 137 m further on, 3.5 … 4.5 m from the right edge – it leaves only 5.6 … 8 m of the track's 10 m between itself and the left edge. edges.right here is the track's own outer line (the full width, as before and after), NOT that solid line. line_in_track: the solid line (its lane side) at the sections line_in_track_sections, should the app want to paint it.

low.why: left edge only: in the 2026 photo a pure white band 1.4 m wide lies over the kerb here (the kerb being repainted or rebuilt before the season) and reaches 0.4 m further into the track than the white line of 2024 and 2025; the edge given is the line of 2024 / 2025 (the two agree within 0.05 m) – where the line is today is not known
